items.title: Add the Sentry connector (#820)
items.body:
## What
Adds the official declarative Sentry connector to Switch Core's service connections catalog.

## Why
Enables operators and developers to connect their Sentry account in Switch Console so agents can inspect error issues, view stack traces, examine crash events, and check releases directly within Switch collaborative rooms.

## Details
- Follows the declarative `adapter: api_key` pattern documented in `docs/design/service-connections-v2.md`.
- **Identity Check:** Validates against `https://sentry.io/api/0/users/me/` with `Authorization: Bearer {api_key}`, mapping account ID (`id`) and label (`email`).
- **MCP Server:** Connects to Sentry's official remote MCP server at `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp` with the documented `Authorization: Sentry-Bearer {api_key}` header.
- **Skill Guide:** Describes investigation workflows for exceptions, stack traces, and releases with safe read-first defaults and confirmation before mutations.
- **Console UI:** Includes official Simple Icons `sentry.svg` vector icon and attribution in `NOTICE.md`.
- **Tests:** Full unit test coverage in `test_loader.py` validating schema compliance.

Closes #820

items.title: feat(connections): add Sentry connector (#820)
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a Sentry connector to Switch using Sentry's official remote MCP server and OAuth authentication.

The integration allows the Switch connector architecture to expose Sentry's diagnostic tools to authorised agents, with verified account identity handling, credential boundaries, and agent safety instructions.

Related to #820.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Switch Console"] --> B["Sentry OAuth Connection"]
    B --> C["OAuth Registration and PKCE"]
    C --> D["Sentry Authorization"]
    D --> E["MCP Identity Verification"]
    E --> F["Switch Connection"]
    F --> G["Agent Grant"]
    G --> H["Session Host MCP Proxy"]
    H --> I["Sentry Remote MCP Server"]
    I --> J["Issues, Events, Stack Traces, Releases"]
```

## Implementation

* Added an enabled Sentry connector catalog entry.
* Integrated the official remote MCP endpoint at `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`.
* Implemented OAuth dynamic registration and structured MCP identity verification.
* Used the required `tools: { mode: pass_through }` configuration.
* Configured an honestly described write-capable access level rather than claiming unverified read-only restrictions.
* Added reusable MCP identity handling and related OAuth, loader, registry, and flow changes.
* Added the Sentry investigation skill for issues, events, stack traces, and releases.
* Added the official Sentry SVG, attribution, and Console integration.
* Added tests for authentication, catalog configuration, identity validation, and security boundaries.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Focused Sentry tests | 33 passed |
| Broader Core tests | 485 passed; one lifecycle fixture initially failed |
| Corrected lifecycle fixture | Passed in focused rerun |
| Python lint and formatting | Passed |
| Mypy | Passed |
| Console builds and typechecks | Passed |
| Console logo tests | 38 passed |
| Agent-provider tests | 946 passed, 8 skipped |
| Live OAuth metadata discovery | Passed |

The full broader Core suite was not reported as rerun after the lifecycle fixture correction.

## Security

* Enforces HTTPS, PKCE, strict identity validation, and bounded responses.
* Rejects unexpected redirects during identity verification.
* Sanitises authentication errors.
* Preserves existing token-lifetime limits.
* Provides safety guidance for sensitive diagnostics and destructive operations.

## Known limitation: OAuth refresh

Sentry's current OAuth refresh behaviour may produce tokens whose lifetime exceeds Switch's enforced lifetime cap.

Switch continues rejecting tokens outside its accepted lifetime policy. Automatic refresh therefore requires additional live verification and may need a separately reviewed compatibility solution.

## Outstanding acceptance criteria

* Credentialed Sentry sign-in.
* Real agent MCP tool execution from a room.
* Successful token renewal.
* Grant removal and disconnect behaviour.
* Transcript/log credential-disclosure checks.
* Requested end-to-end demonstration video.

## Commit

`f53b588b`

This PR includes the implementation and local validation, but should remain a draft until the refresh-compatibility risk and live acceptance requirements are addressed.

items.title: feat(connections): add the Sentry connector (#820)
items.body:
Closes #820

## What this changes

Adds the Sentry connector to Switch's service connection catalog under `core/switch_core/connections/catalog/sentry/`, allowing agents to inspect Sentry issues, events, stack traces, and releases through Sentry's remote MCP server at `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`.

### Why `adapter: api_key`

Issue #820 specifies preferring OAuth with Dynamic Client Registration (DCR) where available, then a static OAuth app, then a key, and explaining the choice in the PR:

1. While `mcp.sentry.dev` advertises OAuth with DCR, it does not provide an RFC 7662 token introspection endpoint or an OIDC `/userinfo` REST endpoint to query identity.
2. Upstream `https://sentry.io/api/0/users/me/` rejects downstream worker OAuth tokens with HTTP 401.
3. Sentry User Auth Tokens are validated directly against `GET https://sentry.io/api/0/users/me/` (`account_id: id`, `label: email`).
4. Sentry MCP natively supports Sentry User Auth Tokens via the `Authorization: Sentry-Bearer {auth_token}` header.
5. This matches Switch's `adapter: api_key` architecture (following the same design as Datadog).

### Included changes

- Added catalog definition `core/switch_core/connections/catalog/sentry/connection.yaml`.
- Added agent skill `core/switch_core/connections/catalog/sentry/skill/SKILL.md` detailing scoped queries, inspecting errors before mutating issues, and data privacy with zero credential references.
- Added vendored Sentry mark at `console/apps/switch-console-desktop/src/assets/images/connections/sentry.svg`.
- Added attribution notice to `console/apps/switch-console-desktop/src/assets/images/connections/NOTICE.md`.
- Registered brand color in `console/apps/switch-console-desktop/src/renderer/features/switch-servers/connection-icon.tsx`.
- Added Sentry to `console/packages/agent-providers/src/host/service-notices.ts`.
- Added catalog loader unit tests in `core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_loader.py` and registry tests in `core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_registry.py`.

## How it was tested

- Ran catalog loader unit tests:
  ```bash
  uv run pytest core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_loader.py -v
  ```
  Result: 128 passed.
- Ran registry tests:
  ```bash
  uv run pytest core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_registry.py -k "test_a_key_service" -v
  ```
  Result: passed.
- Ran code style and lint checks:
  ```bash
  uv run ruff check core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_loader.py core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_registry.py
  uv run ruff format --check core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_loader.py core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_registry.py
  ```
  Result: all passed.

items.title: feat(connections): add the Sentry connector (#820)
items.body:
fixes #820 

## What this changes

Adds the Sentry connector to Switch's connection catalog, allowing agents to inspect Sentry issues, events, stack traces, and releases through Sentry's remote MCP server at `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`.

### Why `adapter: api_key` over OAuth
Issue #820 asks to prefer OAuth with dynamic client registration (DCR) where available and explain the chosen shape in the PR:
1. Sentry's MCP server at `mcp.sentry.dev` supports DCR, but it is built on Cloudflare Workers OAuth Provider and issues downstream worker tokens (`userId:grantId:secret`).
2. `mcp.sentry.dev` does not provide an OIDC `/userinfo` endpoint or an RFC 7662 token introspection endpoint. It only exposes a JSON-RPC `whoami` tool over MCP.
3. Upstream `https://sentry.io/api/0/users/me/` rejects downstream worker tokens with HTTP 401, so Switch cannot complete its REST identity verification (`auth.identity`).
4. Sentry MCP natively supports Sentry User Auth Tokens through the `Authorization: Sentry-Bearer <token>` header scheme.
5. Sentry User Auth Tokens are validated directly against `GET https://sentry.io/api/0/users/me/` (`account_id: id`, `label: email`), which matches Switch's `adapter: api_key` pattern (same as Datadog).

### Included changes
- Added catalog definition `core/switch_core/connections/catalog/sentry/connection.yaml`
- Added agent skill `core/switch_core/connections/catalog/sentry/skill/SKILL.md` with guidelines on narrow queries, issue inspection, and data privacy
- Vendored Sentry mark at `console/apps/switch-console-desktop/src/assets/images/connections/sentry.svg` with `fill="currentColor"`
- Added license entry to `console/apps/switch-console-desktop/src/assets/images/connections/NOTICE.md`
- Registered brand color in `console/apps/switch-console-desktop/src/renderer/features/switch-servers/connection-icon.tsx` (`#362D59` with dark theme fallback)
- Added Sentry to `console/packages/agent-providers/src/host/service-notices.ts`
- Added Sentry catalog and header tests to `core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_loader.py`

## How it was tested

1. Ran catalog loader unit tests:
   ```bash
   PYTHONPATH=core pytest --noconftest core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_loader.py
   ```
   Output: `128 passed in 1.71s` (verifies catalog schema, enabled services, token policy, and MCP request headers).

2. Ran connection icon test suite:
   ```bash
   cd console && pnpm --filter @switch-console/desktop test connection-icon.test.ts
   ```
   Output: `38 passed in 935ms` (verifies logo presence, SVG attributes, and NOTICE.md entries).

3. Ran TypeScript checks across console packages:
   ```bash
   cd console && pnpm -r run typecheck
   ```
   Output: `Done` across all 8 workspace packages with zero errors.

4. Tested live MCP endpoint authentication:
   Sent a JSON-RPC ping to `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp` using `Authorization: Sentry-Bearer <token>` and `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`.
   The endpoint returned `HTTP/2 200 OK` with SSE payload `data: {"result":{},"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1}`.

5. Tested live identity endpoint:
   Queried `GET https://sentry.io/api/0/users/me/` without credentials; received `HTTP/2 401 Unauthorized` with `www-authenticate: Bearer realm="api"`, confirming the endpoint validates Bearer tokens for identity mapping.

items.body:
Closes #820

## Summary

Adds the official Sentry service connection to the Switch connection catalog, closing #820.

### Maintainer Mandate Alignment (Issue #820)
In accordance with maintainer guidance from @petr-sandbox on Issue #820 and `service-connections-v2.md`:
- Configures `adapter: oauth` with `registration: dynamic` and `redirect: [loopback]` on ports 39231-39235.
- Uses `tools: { mode: pass_through }` as required for OAuth entries by the loader.
- Scopes strictly aligned with `https://mcp.sentry.dev/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`:
  - `read`: strictly `org:read` to permit issue search and trace inspection.
  - `write`: `org:read`, `project:write`, `team:write`, `event:write`, `alerts:write`.
  - Administrative deletion capability (`event:admin`) is explicitly omitted to enforce least privilege.
- Documents the 8-hour (`28800`s) token lifetime provenance observed from the authorization server.
- The connection skill (`SKILL.md`) enforces operational safety rules: read-before-write on issues, narrowing time windows, summarizing stack traces rather than dumping raw payloads containing PII, requiring explicit human confirmation before mutating or resolving issues, and indirect prompt injection defense.

### Changes Included
1. **Catalog Entry:** `core/switch_core/connections/catalog/sentry/connection.yaml`
2. **Connection Skill:** `core/switch_core/connections/catalog/sentry/skill/SKILL.md` (clean, idiomatic, matching `datadog` / `atlassian`)
3. **Desktop Assets & Color Tokens:**
   - Vendored Simple Icons SVG logo: `console/apps/switch-console-desktop/src/assets/images/connections/sentry.svg`
   - Attribution notice in `NOTICE.md`
   - Brand color mapping in `connection-icon.tsx` (`sentry: 'text-[#362D59] emdark:text-foreground'`)
4. **Test Suite Enhancements:**
   - `core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_loader.py`: Shipped catalog entry tests, skill validation, scope assertions.
   - `core/tests/switch_core/connections/test_registry.py`: Dynamic client registration and scope configuration tests.
   - `core/tests/switch_core/gateway/test_connection_catalog.py`: Catalog listing status assertion.

items.title: add the Sentry connector
items.body:
Adds the Sentry connector (#820): an `oauth` catalog entry plus a skill.

## Shape

Sentry's hosted MCP server (`https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`) advertises OAuth dynamic client registration and a discoverable revocation endpoint, so Core registers its own client and discovers the endpoints. Self-hosted Sentry is out of scope.

## Least access

Read asks for `org:read`; write adds `project:write`, `team:write`, `event:write` and `alerts:write`. No member-management or org-admin scopes.

## How it was tested

`just check`, `just typecheck` and the loader and registry test suites pass. Added the shipped-entry assertions to `test_loader.py` and the registry adapter set.

items.title: Add the Sentry connector
items.body:
Closes #820.

## Video

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25350b8a-e23d-4e84-9f36-2821056e6c61

Connect from Switch Console, Sentry's consent screen, grant to an agent, the agent looks up Sentry issues from a Mattermost room, the grant turned off and the agent loses access, then disconnect.

## What this changes

Sentry becomes a connector in the first shape, a remote MCP server with OAuth: `https://mcp.sentry.dev/mcp`, with dynamic client registration, so nothing is set up on the server.

- `core/switch_core/connections/catalog/sentry/connection.yaml` and `skill/SKILL.md`
- `console/.../assets/images/connections/sentry.svg`, the official mark (Simple Icons 16.33.0, viewBox and path only), credited in `NOTICE.md`, coloured `#362D59` and white in the dark theme (`connection-icon.tsx`)
- `service-notices.ts`: notices name it "Sentry", like the other live connectors
- `docs/design/service-connections-v2.md`: a Sentry section, and `identity.mcp_tool` and `token.note` in the catalog schema and "Adding a connector"
- `token.note` (loader), sent as `agent_access_note` by `GET /service-connections` and shown by Switch Console on the connector's page and in its connect dialog: how the one-hour limit below is made clear in Console

### Why one small loader and adapter change

The catalog alone cannot connect Sentry. I measured the sign-in against sentry.io before writing the entry:

| Measured | Result |
|---|---|
| Token answer | `access_token`, `token_type`, `expires_in: 3600`, `scope`, `refresh_token`, `resource`. No user. |
| `GET https://sentry.io/api/0/users/me/` with the MCP token | **401**. The token works with the MCP server alone. |
| `GET https://sentry.io/api/0/` with the MCP token | **401** as well. |
| MCP `whoami` tool | `structuredContent.user` with `id`, `email`, `name`. |

Every identity URL on sentry.io refuses the token, so an entry that reads the account with a GET can never finish connecting: Switch says "Sentry refused the sign-in. Connect again." So `ConnectionIdentity` gains one optional field, `mcp_tool`. With it, `url` must be one of the entry's own MCP servers (the loader checks this), and `OAuthAdapter.identify` opens a short MCP session there (`initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/call`, then `DELETE` of the session), reads the tool's `structuredContent` (or the first text content that is a JSON object), and takes `account_id` and `label` from it as before. JSON and event-stream answers are both read; a 401 still asks for a new sign-in. Every other entry is unchanged: without `mcp_tool` the GET path accepts 200 only, as before.

### Access levels

Sentry's consent screen asks which skills to allow: Inspect Issues & Events (48 read-only tools), Seer (18), Triage Issues (26), Manage Projects & Teams (25). I signed in with different choices and the granted scopes were the same four every time (`org:read project:write team:write event:write`). The choice limits the tools on Sentry's side, and Sentry remembers it for the next sign-in.

So, as the [guidance on #820](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/issues/820#issuecomment-6596711549) asks for a vendor whose scopes cannot make a connection read-only, Sentry is offered at **one level, read and write**, labelled honestly. The loader needs a `read` block, so it lists the same scopes; Switch asks for the write scopes, every connection is granted the write level, and Console labels it "Read and write" (as in the video). Nothing is ever labelled read-only. The entry and the skill say the connection can write, and the skill names what each of Sentry's skills can change. A person who wants an agent that only reads allows Inspect alone on Sentry's consent screen, which limits the tools on Sentry's side. The skill tells the agent that a missing tool was not allowed, and to say so rather than look for another way. `alerts:write` is not asked for.

### Other choices

| Choice | Why |
|---|---|
| OAuth with dynamic registration | The issue's first preference, and Sentry offers it (PKCE S256, revocation at its token endpoint). The token header shape would make people paste a long-lived key. |
| Loopback redirect, Atlassian's five ports | Connects from Switch Console, so a server without a public address can connect Sentry too. No new redirect hosts. |
| `max_lifetime: 3600` | The first token's `expires_in: 3600`, measured. Refreshed tokens: see the known limit below. |
| `refresh: rotating` | A refresh after the first token expired worked with no new sign-in (the connection's secret revision went from 1 to 2). Rotating keeps whatever refresh token comes back, so it is right whether or not Sentry rotates. |
| Sentry.io only | A self-hosted Sentry needs the local MCP server, which the issue puts out of scope. |

## Known limit: agents have Sentry for the hour after each sign-in

Found by leaving a connection past its first hour, and confirmed in Sentry's own source:

- The first access token lives 3600 s.
- Sentry's MCP server never refreshes upstream. A refresh re-issues a token that lives as long as the person's 30-day Sentry token has left (`tokenExchangeCallback` in [getsentry/sentry-mcp](https://github.com/getsentry/sentry-mcp/blob/main/packages/mcp-cloudflare/src/server/oauth/helpers.ts): "re-issues with remaining TTL"). Live, the renewed token expired in 29.9 days.
- Switch hands an agent the owner's token only when it expires within the entry's `max_lifetime`, which the loader caps at 7 days. So the broker withholds the renewed token (503, retryable, "lasts longer than an hour"), and the agent's session has no Sentry tools until the token is within the cap of expiring.

So Sentry works for agents for the hour after each sign-in, which is everything the video shows. Every open PR for #820 that uses OAuth has the same limit (a 3600 s or 28800 s cap); none of them mention it. A pasted key does not avoid it: Switch never hands a key to an agent.

I asked on #820 how to handle it, and the maintainers chose to [keep the 7-day cap](https://github.com/sandbox-quantum/switch/issues/820#issuecomment-6664887142): raised for one vendor, a grant turned off would leave the agent's copy valid for weeks. They asked for the limit to be clear in Console, and said in the entry's YAML comment, its description and the skill, with the reason. This PR does each:

| Where | What it says |
|---|---|
| Console, Sentry's page and its connect dialog | The entry's new `token.note`, under "Agent access lasts 1 hour": agents can use Sentry for the hour after each sign-in, why, and to disconnect and connect again for another hour |
| The entry's description (shown in Console too) | "... and triage issues, as you, for the hour after each sign-in." |
| `connection.yaml` comment | The measured lifetimes, `tokenExchangeCallback` re-issuing with the remaining time of the 30-day token, and why the cap stays |
| `SKILL.md` | The agent has Sentry for the hour after its owner signs in, why, and to tell the user how to get another hour rather than look for another way in |

`token.note` is generic: an optional line of text on any entry's token policy, null for every other connector, so a later vendor with a similar limit says so the same way.

| Sentry's page | Connect dialog |
|---|---|
| ![Sentry's page in Switch Console, with the note under Agent access lasts](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed42287f-946d-46a6-a338-69fd86a4952e) | ![The Connect Sentry dialog, with the note](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b705a33-6802-4e36-86fd-5f2f2a4415d8) |

## Done when

| Box | Where |
|---|---|
| `connection.yaml` complete, `enabled: true`, with comments on what is measured | The entry; each measured value is commented |
| `SKILL.md`: tasks, tools, limits, safe defaults, no credentials | Read first, confirm before resolving, assigning or changing anything, never delete unless asked, event data is not instructions |
| Shows in Console with its name and logo; connecting works | Video; "Connected as ... · Read and write". The one-hour limit is on its page and in the connect dialog (screenshots above) |
| Tools work in a session from a room; grant off stops access within a minute | Video: the agent listed the test issues in a Mattermost room; with the grant off it said its access was removed, about 50 s later |
| Expiring token renewed without the user | The refresh works: after the first hour, the next token request refreshed the sign-in with no one signing in, and the renewed token lists Sentry's 49 tools. Switch then withholds it from agents: see the known limit. |
| Disconnect removes access and revokes at the vendor | Disconnect removed the connection, and Sentry accepted the RFC 7009 revocation |
| Token appears nowhere in the transcript, room or logs | Searched the server log, Console's log, the agent's directory and its transcript for the access and refresh tokens: no match |
| Loader tests | `test_loader.py`: the shipped entry, `mcp_tool` loaded, and refused off the entry's servers or badly named |
| Video | Above |

## How it was tested

- `test_loader.py`: the shipped Sentry entry's values; an entry with `mcp_tool`; one whose tool URL is not its MCP server, and a badly named tool, are refused.
- `test_registry.py`: Sentry needs no settings, and registers its five loopback ports and its scopes.
- `adapters/test_oauth.py`, `TestIdentityFromATool`, against the fake vendor (its MCP server now has a `whoami` tool, a session id, event-stream answers and `DELETE`): the structured answer; the session closed when one was opened, and nothing sent when none was; an event-stream answer; the text fallback; an answer without JSON refused; a failed tool refused with its session still closed; a refused token asks for a new sign-in; a down server is unavailable; the GET path still accepts 200 only.
- `test_loader.py` also checks the shipped entry's `token.note` and description name the one-hour limit; `gateway/test_service_connections.py` checks the list sends Sentry's note as `agent_access_note`, and null for another service.
- Console: `gateway-client.test.ts` reads `agent_access_note` from the server, and null from an older one; `service-connect-step.test.tsx` shows the note in the connect dialog, and nothing more for a service without one.
- `test_loader.py`, `test_registry.py`, `adapters/test_oauth.py` and `gateway/test_service_connections.py`: 245 passed. The one other, `test_rejects_a_symlink_in_a_skill`, needs symlink rights my Windows machine does not grant, and fails the same way on `main`.
- Console: the six node test files that build catalog entries, 281 passed; the five browser test files that do, 44 passed.
- `ruff format --check`, `ruff check`, `mypy switch_core/connections switch_core/gateway/service_connections.py`: clean. Console: `tsgo --noEmit` for the desktop app and `agent-providers`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed files, and the `agent-providers` host tests.
- By hand, against sentry.io with a test organization and three test errors (a `KeyError`, a `ZeroDivisionError` and a `ValueError` in release `checkout@1.4.2`), from Switch Console and a Mattermost room, as in the video.
